tb-207-1.question:
A pole vault athlete passes the bar with the aid of a pole (Fig a) and is about to land on a mat.

Which of the following is/are the reason(s) why the mat can protect the athlete from injury?

(1) The mat reduces the change in momentum of the athlete during impact.

(2) The mat reduces the rate of change in momentum of the athlete during impact.

(3) The mat deforms when the athlete lands on it.

A (1) only

B (2) only

C (1) and (3) only

D (2) and (3) only
tb-207-1.reasoning:
Stopping from the same landing velocity produces the same momentum change, so the mat does not reduce Δp and (1) is false. The mat deforms, extending the stopping time.

From average resultant force F=Δp/Δt, the longer time reduces the rate of momentum change and the average impact force. Statements (2) and (3) are correct: D.

tb-207-8.question:

B M2

tb-207-8.reasoning:
The free-body diagrams for the two monkeys are shown below.

The monkeys fall for the same height, so they have the same speed just before collision. The time of impact is the same, so the net force acting on them in the collision is the same.

tb-207-10.question:
Object X collides head-on with object Y which is initially at rest, on a smooth horizontal plane. The mass of X is m and it moves at a speed u before the collision. The mass of Y is M and it moves at a speed v after the collision. Which of the following statements is/are correct?

(1) Mv can be larger than mu.

(2) v can be larger than u.

(3) Mv2 can be larger than mu2.

A (2) only

B (1) and (2) only

C (1) and (3) only

D (1), (2) and (3)
tb-207-10.reasoning:
Consider elastic collision.

Let vX be the speed of X after collision.

By the law of conservation of momentum,

mu + 0 = mvX + Mv

vX =mu−Mvm (1)

By the law of conservation of energy,

12mu2 +0 =12mvX2 + 12Mv2

mu2 = mvX2 + Mv2 (2)

Put (1) into (2),

mu2 = m(mu−Mvm)2 + Mv2

mu2 = mu2 – 2Muv +M2v2m+ Mv2

0 =v2 − 2Muv

0 =[(M+mm)v−2u]Mv

v =(2mM+m)u

If M is smaller than m, then v is larger than u.

∴ (2) is correct.

v =(2mM+m)u

Mv =(2MM+m)mu

If M is larger than m, then Mv is larger than mu.

∴ (1) is correct.

By the law of conservation of energy, the final KE of Y must not be larger than the total initial KE, i.e. the initial KE of X.

12Mv2 ≤ 12mu2

Mv2 ≤ mu2

∴ (3) is incorrect.

tb-207-35.question:
A water wheel turns when a stream of water hits the paddles (Fig ah).

Fig ah

(a) A force acts on the paddle when it is hit by a stream of water. Explain this by considering the momentum of the water. (3 marks)

(b) If curved paddles are used, water can leave the paddle in the opposite direction (Fig ai).

(i) Explain why the curved paddle results in a larger force when it is hit by the same stream of water. (1 mark)

(ii) Suppose water flows at a rate of 5 kg s−1 into a fixed curved paddle. The water enters the paddle at 10 m s−1 towards the right and leaves at the same speed towards the left. Find the force acting on the paddle by the water. (2 marks)
tb-207-35.answer:
(a) When water hits the paddle, its momentum changes. 1A

The net force acting on the water is its rate of change in momentum. 1A

By Newton’s third law of motion, a reaction force of the same magnitude acts on the paddle by the water in the opposite direction. 1A

(b) (i) The change in momentum of the water is larger. 1A

(ii) Consider the water.

F =mv−mut

=mt(v−u)

= 5 × [10 − (−10)] 1M

= 100 N

By Newton’s third law of motion, the force acting on the paddle by the water is 100 N. 1A

Let pA and pB be the magnitude of the momentum of A and B after the explosion.

By the law of conservation of momentum,

pA = pB

By the law of conservation of energy,

KEA + KEB = EPE

pA22mA+pB22mB = 5

pA22×0.5+pA22×1.5 = 5 1M

pA = 1.936 kg m s−1

Speed of A =pAmA=1.9360.5= 3.87 m s−1
